summary: REST write-plan entrypoints that expose app orchestration outputs for implemented messenger, mail, social, and community write routes.
claim_boundary: REST-to-app write-plan bridge only. Existing receipt handlers remain; new entrypoints return app plans with persistence commands and protocol envelopes but still do not execute SQL, publish broker events, serve gRPC, or deploy a runtime gateway.

facets.F1_simplicity: Each REST crate adds a narrow write-plan function over existing REST request/context shapes and the app orchestration crate for that service.
facets.F2_hyperscaler: Gateway-facing boundaries can now obtain validated receipt, persistence, and protocol event plans from one call, reducing integration drift before cloud runtime wiring. Runtime execution and SLO evidence remain pending.
facets.F3_adversarial: Tests verify every implemented write route returns persistence statements and proto-bound protocol events, including community vote and moderation paths.
facets.F5_quality: Focused REST tests plus broad 27-package cargo check/test/clippy/fmt, dependency-seam, honest-claims, and diff hygiene are part of this evidence run.
facets.F7_security_privacy: REST write-plan entrypoints preserve the same API validation and policy/idempotency/audit fields as receipt-only handlers while delegating scope drift checks to app plans.
facets.F11_observability: REST write-plan responses preserve audit correlation IDs in app persistence/protocol plans for future gateway telemetry and audit-chain integration.
